title: Di Cosmo 2021 · Resting MEG and PPS boundary
citation: Di Cosmo et al. (2021). Phase-coupling of neural oscillations contributes to individual differences in peripersonal space. Neuropsychologia, 156, 107823.
notes: Published study settings are available for inspection. See the source-backed method and remaining execution requirements.

published_method.relationship: The behavioral PPS task, resting MEG and supporting structural MRI used separate days with the same enrolled cohort. Correlate resting connectivity with each participant's behavioral looming sigmoid midpoint.
published_method.acquisition: ITAB whole-head system with 153 dcSQUID magnetometers and concurrent ECG and EOG. Five head coils track positioning. Digitize fiducials and locate the head after each run.
published_method.structural_coregistration: Individual T1 supports a one-shell inner-skull BEM. Apply weighted minimum-norm source estimates on a 4 mm grid with three components per voxel.
published_method.analysis: Compute seed-to-voxel Multivariate Interaction Measure from left premotor cortex (Talairach −51, −10, 20 mm) with a left primary auditory control seed (−39, −31, 12 mm). Pearson correlations relate band-limited connectivity to the individual PPS midpoint.
published_method.analysis_discrepancy: The Figure 2B printed correlation is positive, while its plotted relationship, caption and Results describe a negative association.

implementation_gaps: Requires timed silent rest blocks, clinical-grade MEG with ECG/EOG, participant-specific structural coregistration and a validated source connectivity pipeline.
Acquisition sampling and filters, artifact rejection thresholds, spectral windows and exact correlation correction settings remain unresolved.
reference_parameters.planner_scope: The study settings describe the source procedure. The Planner contains no executable trial schedule for this profile.
